````json
{
  "name": "pipeline_chain explanation",
  "overview": "`pipeline_chain.py` is a small shared Airflow helper that lets ExternalTaskSensors match the latest successful upstream DAG run on the same calendar day (Asia/Dubai), instead of requiring an exact logical_date match.",
  "plan": "# Explanation of `pipeline_chain.py`\n\n[`employee_data/flows/pipeline_chain.py`](employee_data/flows/pipeline_chain.py) is **not a DAG**. It is a shared module used by other employee pipelines so cross-DAG sensors still work when DAGs are triggered **manually** on the same calendar day but with **different `logical_date` timestamps**.\n\n## Why it exists\n\nAirflow’s `ExternalTaskSensor` defaults to waiting for an upstream task whose `logical_date` equals the current run’s `logical_date`. That works for aligned schedules. Manual triggers often get a unique timestamp even if they are started on the same Dubai calendar day, so an exact match never finds the upstream run.\n\nThis module replaces that exact match with: **latest successful upstream `end` task whose DAG run falls on the same Dubai day**.\n\n## How the two functions work\n\n**`same_day_latest_success_execution_date_fn(external_dag_id, external_task_id)`** returns an `execution_date_fn` for `ExternalTaskSensor`.\n\nOn each poke it:\n\n1. Takes the current DAG’s `logical_date`.\n2. Interprets the day in **Asia/Dubai** (if the timestamp is UTC). If timezone conversion fails, it still uses a pendulum instance of `logical_date`.\n3. Converts that day’s start/end to UTC (`day_start` inclusive, `day_end` exclusive).\n4. Queries Airflow metadata: join `DagRun` to `TaskInstance` where:\n   - DAG = `external_dag_id`\n   - task = `external_task_id`\n   - task state = `SUCCESS`\n   - `DagRun.execution_date` in `[day_start, day_end)`\n5. Returns the **latest** matching `execution_date`. If none exist, it returns the original `logical_date` (sensor then waits / fails as usual).\n\nThe query uses `DagRun.execution_date`, not `logical_date`. In Airflow 2.10, `logical_date` is a **read-only Python alias** and is not a SQLAlchemy column; filtering on it previously crashed.\n\n**`upstream_sensor_kwargs(...)`** is a convenience dict for sensors:\n\n- `mode`: `poke` (polls every interval; does not free the worker slot like `reschedule`)\n- `poke_interval`: 60 seconds\n- `timeout`: 7200 seconds (2 hours)\n- `failed_states`: `[\"failed\"]` — if the matched upstream task failed, this sensor fails instead of hanging\n- `execution_date_fn`: the same-day lookup above\n\n## Where it is used\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  leave_data[\"leave_data end\"]\n  onsite[\"onsite_employee\"]\n  emp[\"employee_data\"]\n  saal[\"saal_model\"]\n\n  leave_data --\u003e onsite\n  onsite --\u003e|\"wait_leave then TriggerDagRun\"| emp\n  leave_data --\u003e emp\n  onsite --\u003e emp\n  emp --\u003e|\"end then TriggerDagRun\"| saal\n```\n\n- [`onsite_employee_flow.py`](employee_data/flows/onsite_employee_flow.py): after `end`, `wait_leave_data` uses `upstream_sensor_kwargs(\"leave_data\", \"end\")`, then `TriggerDagRunOperator` starts `employee_data` with the same `logical_date`.\n- [`employee_data.py`](employee_data/flows/employee_data.py): before `start`, waits on `leave_data.end` and `onsite_employee.end` with the same helper, then after `end` triggers `saal_model`.\n\nThe trigger operators themselves are **not** in this file. They live on the DAG files (`wait_for_completion=False`, `reset_dag_run=True`). This module only solves **sensor date matching**.\n\n## Behaviour notes\n\n- “Same day” is **Dubai calendar day**, then converted to UTC for the DB query.\n- Multiple successful upstream runs on that day: the **latest** `execution_date` wins.\n- No successful run that day: sensor keeps looking at the current `logical_date` until timeout.\n- Callers still pass `external_dag_id` / `external_task_id` on the sensor; `upstream_sensor_kwargs` repeats those IDs only for the lookup function.\n"
}
````
